sources.citation: Michael A. Goodman, "Religion and Perfectionism," BYU Studies Quarterly 63(4), 2024 - high-toxic-perfectionism group rates by religious affiliation, and the high- vs. low-perfectionism introjected-motivation split, from the Foundations longitudinal panel (2,000+ youth in Utah, Arizona, and California).

Michael A. Goodman, "Religion and Perfectionism," BYU Studies Quarterly 63(4), 2024, Figure 1, "Perfectionism (Socially Prescribed, and Discrepancy) by Religious Identity" - full Low/Mid-Low/Mid/Mid-High/High distribution by religious-identity group, from the same Foundations longitudinal panel.

high-perfectionism-by-group.unit: percent of each group in the high-toxic-perfectionism category

perfectionism-distribution-by-group.unit: percent of each group falling in each perfectionism band (rows sum to ~100, rounding)

introjected-motivation.unit: percent in the high-introjected-motivation (guilt/shame-driven religion) group
